generation.explanation: A radian is the angle at the center of a circle created by an arc whose length equals the circle's radius. If you wrap the radius along the circumference, the central angle you get is exactly 1 radian. A full circle is 2π radians (about 6.28), which is why π appears throughout formulas involving angles and circles.
